title: Legal review: benchmark claims, substantiation packet, and required disclaimers for public release
creator: Soojin Lee
description:
Objective
- Obtain Legal approval (claims + disclaimers + substantiation) for all public-facing benchmark assets: landing page, interactive table tooltips, PDF report, blog post, press kit, and sales enablement talk track.
- Ensure we use consistent, legally safe language for comparative and performance claims, and retain the source-of-truth data needed for substantiation.

In scope
- Claim inventory and risk rating (absolute claims vs comparative claims vs descriptive statements)
- Substantiation packet requirements (data, methodology, versions, configs, retention)
- Required disclaimers/footnotes (methodology limitations, variance, competitor baseline caveats)
- Approval workflow + final sign-off checkpoint before publish

Links / artifacts
- Confluence legal guidelines: sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/benchmark-claims-legal-review-guidelines.json
- Data retention policy: sources/confluence/policies-and-process/data-management/public-benchmark-data-retention-policy.json
- Methodology (canonical): sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/latency-per-dollar-benchmark-methodology.json
- Validation checklist: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/benchmark-data-validation-and-review-checklist.json
- Messaging/message house (must align): sources/confluence/sales-enablement/positioning-and-messaging/benchmark-report-core-message-house.json
- Docs PR w/ landing copy + disclaimers: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-3912-add-benchmark-report-landing-page-and-disclaimers.json

Owners / reviewers
- DRI (PMM): Soojin Lee
- Legal: Michael Grant (primary), Sofia Mendes (comparative language)
- Security review partner: Naomi Feldman (public artifact redaction / operational sensitivity)
- Bench leads for substantiation: Jonas Weber, Claire Dubois, Rina Kobayashi

Deliverables
1) Claim matrix (source asset -> exact wording -> required substantiation -> approval status)
2) Final approved disclaimer blocks (short + long versions) for:
   - Landing page header/footer
   - Interactive table tooltip / ‘How we measured’ modal
   - PDF methodology + appendix footnotes
   - Sales enablement FAQ (what we can/can’t say)
3) Substantiation packet stored in the internal retention location with access control and a clear ‘public numbers’ hash/version reference.

Acceptance criteria
- All public assets marked ‘Approved’ in claim matrix and frozen prior to launch.
- No disallowed phrases remain in docs/press/email/talk track (see ‘Disallowed / risky phrasing’ section below).
- Substantiation packet includes: run manifests, model versions, regions, hardware class, concurrency, caching/batching policy, metric definitions, exclusion criteria, and rerun thresholds.
- Retention plan acknowledged by Applied ML + Marketing Ops (who stores what, for how long, who can access).

Disallowed / risky phrasing (guidance)
- Absolute superlatives without qualification: “fastest”, “best”, “#1”, “most reliable”, “lowest cost”
- Over-broad comparative claims: “X is 2x cheaper than competitors” without stating competitor set, methodology, and dates
- Over-promising consistency: “guaranteed p95” if not an SLA / if data shows variance
- Claims implying third-party endorsement unless explicitly true

Approved / safer framing patterns
- “In our testing on Redwood Inference (date range), using the methodology described here…”
- “Results will vary by workload, context length, output length, and region capacity.”
- “Competitor baselines are provided for context where available; they are not exhaustive and were measured under the stated conditions.”
- “Latency/$ is a composite metric; see definitions and raw metrics (p50/p95, $/1M tokens) for details.”

Milestones
- M1: Claim inventory + redlines from Legal on draft copy (target: 2025-06-18)
- M2: Substantiation packet draft complete (target: 2025-06-24)
- M3: Final disclaimers + final review of landing page/PDF/blog/press kit (target: 2025-07-02)
- M4: Sign-off + publish freeze (target: 2025-07-07)

Notes
- This ticket is a launch blocker. If Legal flags a claim as ‘high risk’ without sufficient substantiation, we will either (a) soften language, (b) add a qualifier, or (c) remove claim from asset.
comments: 2025-06-12 (Soojin Lee): Created ticket. Pulling together initial claim inventory from landing page v1 + report outline. Requesting Legal to confirm required disclaimer minimums for landing page vs PDF vs press kit.

2025-06-14 (Michael Grant): Confirmed we need (1) clear methodology link adjacent to any performance claim, (2) date range of measurements, (3) statement that results vary by workload/region/capacity. Comparative claims require a defined competitor set and non-misleading presentation of differences. Please share exact chart captions and any ‘topline’ callouts you want to use in PR/email.

2025-06-18 (Soojin Lee): Uploaded claim matrix draft (v0.3) to internal doc. Key question: can we say “better latency/$ than leading managed endpoints” if we only include 2 vendors? Tentative: no—will replace with “competitive baselines shown for context” and keep it footnoted.

2025-06-20 (Sofia Mendes): Comparative language guidance: avoid “leading” and “industry standard” unless you define it. Prefer “selected third-party endpoints measured under the conditions described.” Also avoid implying that competitor numbers reflect their ‘best possible’ tuning. Add: “We did not apply vendor-specific optimizations beyond documented defaults.”

2025-06-24 (Michael Grant): Legal claims review meeting notes: (a) Remove ‘up to 3x’ callout unless we keep it tightly scoped to model+region+workload and show the distribution; (b) add explicit definition of ‘latency/$’ and what costs are included/excluded; (c) ensure any mention of reliability references actual SLOs or is phrased as observational (“lower variance in our runs”).

2025-06-26 (Naomi Feldman): Security review: ensure public artifacts do not expose internal cluster IDs, fleet sizing, or customer identifiers. OK to publish region names and broad hardware class (e.g., “H100-class”) but avoid exact instance counts. Confirm redaction pass is in the validation checklist and that raw logs remain access-controlled.

2025-07-01 (Soojin Lee): Incorporated Legal redlines into landing page + report captions. Replaced superlatives with qualified language. Added ‘results vary’ disclaimer to interactive table footer + ‘How we measured’ modal. Pending final review once charts are finalized.

2025-07-02 (Michael Grant): Reviewed updated draft copy + disclaimers. Remaining change requests: (1) Put measurement window (e.g., “Measured June 2025”) in the PDF executive summary footer; (2) add a note that pricing inputs for $/1M tokens are Redwood list prices as of measurement date; (3) remove the phrase “apples-to-apples” (too strong).

2025-07-07 (Soojin Lee): Freeze candidate sent for final sign-off: landing page copy, PDF v1.0, blog draft, press kit boilerplate, and sales one-pager. Claim matrix updated to v1.0 with required substantiation links.

2025-07-09 (Michael Grant): Approved with conditions met. Final disclaimer block is acceptable. Substantiation packet must be retained per policy and accessible for 24 months. Any post-launch edits to numeric claims or competitor references require re-review.

2025-07-10 (Soojin Lee): Marking Done. Shared approved language with PM-839 (enablement kit) and redwood-docs PR reviewers. Added note to runbook that any “benchmark refresh” or new model addendum needs a new claim matrix pass.
final_approved_disclaimer_block_short: Benchmark results are based on Redwood Inference testing conducted during the stated measurement window using the published methodology. Results will vary by workload (prompt/output lengths, concurrency), model versions, regional capacity, and configuration. Latency/$ is a composite metric; see methodology for definitions and supporting metrics (p50/p95 latency, throughput, and $/1M tokens).
final_approved_disclaimer_block_competit: Where competitor baselines are shown, they are provided for context and are not exhaustive. Measurements reflect the stated conditions and publicly documented defaults; we did not apply undocumented vendor-specific optimizations. Differences may be driven by hardware, system configuration, routing, or regional capacity at the time of testing.
substantiation_packet_checklist: Required contents: run manifests (hash/versioned), model IDs + versions, regions tested, hardware class, concurrency levels, warmup protocol, caching/batching policy, metric definitions, aggregation method, exclusions/outlier rules, rerun thresholds and stability gates, pricing inputs and date, raw logs location + access controls + retention timeline. Owner: Jonas Weber / Claire Dubois. Storage must comply with public-benchmark-data-retention-policy.
release_notes: Legal sign-off granted for benchmark launch assets (landing page/PDF/blog/press kit/sales enablement) as of 2025-07-09. Any future modifications to numeric comparisons, competitor mentions, or headline performance claims require re-approval.
